    AI Overview
    The British online newspaper The Independent is owned by Independent Digital News & Media Ltd, with Russian billionaire Evgeny Lebedev being a major figure and significant shareholder alongside other investors, though his father Alexander also previously owned it, with the business focusing entirely on digital after ending print in 2016. 
    Key Points:
    • Primary Owner:
      The entity controlling The Independent is Independent Digital News & Media Ltd. 
    • Key Investor:
      Evgeny Lebedev holds a significant stake (around 41%) and is the primary owner figure, though he hasn't been actively involved in operations since 2016, according to a spokesperson. 
    • Previous Ownership:
      Alexander Lebedev (Evgeny's father) acquired the paper in 2010, with the family running it until the print editions ceased in 2016. 
    • Focus:
      Since 2016, The Independent has operated solely as a digital publication.

      AI Overview
      The UK's The Independent newspaper leans centre-left, often described as liberal, aligning with progressive thought, though it aims for centrist appeal, while the US-based The Indypendent is explicitly progressive and left-leaning, covering social justice issues, and another publication, Independent Journal Review (IJR), leans conservative, so context matters. 
      For the UK's The Independent
      • Bias Rating: AllSides rates it as "Lean Left". 
      • General Stance: Generally seen as centre-left, liberal, and supportive of progressive policies, though it strives for broad appeal. 
      • Example Issues: Has campaigned for greater refugee rights and a "Final Say" referendum on Brexit. 
      The Indypendent (NYC) 
      • Bias: Explicitly progressive and left-leaning.
      • Focus: Covers social justice movements, power systems, and issues from a left-wing perspective.
      Independent Journal Review (IJR) 
      • Bias: Conservative.
      • Focus: A US-based news and opinion site covering general topics from a conservative viewpoint.
      In Summary
      When discussing "The Independent," it's crucial to specify whether you mean the UK's centre-left The Independent, the progressive The Indypendent, or the conservative Independent Journal Review.

        AI Overview
        The Independent newspaper generally holds a liberal, centre-left editorial stance, supporting causes like environmentalism and opposing Brexit, while advocating for transparency and holding power accountable, though it aims for impartial news reporting and allows diverse columnist opinions, positioning itself as a digitally focused, values-led publication with a history of challenging mainstream narratives. 
        Key Aspects of its Stance:
        • Political Leaning:
          It's often described as liberal or centre-left, contrasting with more centrist or right-leaning papers, and has strong support for causes like climate action and social justice. 
        • Brexit Stance:
          Famously campaigned for a "Final Say" referendum on Brexit, reflecting strong opposition to leaving the EU. 
        • Impartiality vs. Editorializing:
          While striving for accurate news, The Independent acknowledges its history of campaigning journalism and editorializing on key issues, distinct from its straight news reporting. 
        • Digital Focus:
          After ceasing print in 2016, it became a fully digital platform, focusing on global news, digital storytelling, and audience engagement, becoming a major online news source. 
        • Historical Positions:
          Known for opposing the Iraq War and criticizing US/UK foreign policy, with a history of challenging established narratives. 
        In essence, The Independent aims to be an independent voice, free from partisan affiliation, but its editorial positions lean towards progressive, liberal, and socially conscious viewpoints, particularly on issues like climate change, human rights, and democracy.

          AI Overview
          The online presence of The Independent, a prominent UK-based newspaper, is extensive, shifting to a digital-only model in 2016, featuring a highly trafficked website (independent.co.uk), a strong presence across major social media platforms (X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube), dedicated apps (Independent Daily Edition), and services like Independent Premium, focusing on progressive, trusted journalism for vast global audiences, especially in the U.S., where it's a leading British digital news brand. 
          Key Components of its Online Presence:
          • Website & Apps:
            Their core is the digital newspaper accessible via their website (independent.co.uk) and mobile apps, offering free articles with registration, premium content (Independent Premium), and a daily digital edition. 
          • Social Media Dominance:
            They leverage platforms like X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Threads, and YouTube to reach millions, with significant audience growth in the U.S. 
          • Content Strategy:
            They provide breaking news, in-depth analysis, video content (Independent TV), and lifestyle features, aiming for a trustworthy, unbiased perspective. 
          • U.S. Growth:
            The Independent has seen massive growth in the U.S., becoming a top digital news publisher there, attracting millions of unique visitors. 
          • Community Engagement:
            They support events, forums, and local initiatives, fostering civic engagement online and offline, exemplified by local outlets like The Santa Barbara Independent. 
          Examples of Usage:
          • Accessing News: Readers use the website, apps, and social media for free daily news updates. 
          • In-depth Reading: Subscribers access premium content and the daily digital newspaper. 
          • Video & Events: Viewers watch Independent TV and book tickets for virtual events. 
          • Social Sharing: Users share articles and engage with content across platforms like X, Facebook, and Instagram.

            AI Overview
            The history of The Independent, a prominent British newspaper, traces back to its 1986 launch by former Daily Telegraph journalists, known for its distinctive design, center-left stance, and "free from party political bias" claim, evolving from broadsheet to compact (tabloid) format, facing financial struggles, acquisition by Independent News & Media (Tony O'Reilly), then Russian businessman Alexander Lebedev, and finally transitioning entirely to a digital-only format in 2016 after years of declining print circulation, while other publications named Independent exist, like the U.S. Independent Press-Telegram.
             
            Founding & Early Years (1986-1990s)
            • Launch: First published October 7, 1986, by Andreas Whittam Smith, Stephen Glover, and Matthew Symonds. 
            • Mission: Positioned as an independent voice, free from party political bias, competing with established broadsheets. 
            • Design: Known for innovative, high-quality design, initially in broadsheet format. 
            Growth & Changes (1990s-2000s)
            • Competition:
              Faced price wars with Murdoch's titles, launching campaigns mocking rival ownership. 
            • Format Shift:
              Introduced a compact (tabloid) version in 2003, a move later followed by The Times. 
            • Ownership:
              Acquired by Tony O'Reilly's Independent News & Media in the mid-90s, then by Russian oligarch Alexander Lebedev in 2010. 
            Digital Transition (2010s) 
            • Decline:
              Experienced significant circulation drops despite critical acclaim and awards.
            • Digital Focus:
              Published its final print edition on March 26, 2016, becoming a digital-only publication.
            Other "Independent" Newspapers
            • USA:
              The Independent Press-Telegram in Long Beach, California, a historical local paper. 
            • U.S. Magazine:
              An influential religious/political magazine published in the late 19th/early 20th centuries. 
            • Other Companies:
              Various regional publications also use "Independent" in their names, like Independent Newsmedia Inc. in the U.S.
